question_text:
Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine

Clinical Education Center

**STATION S**

**Presenting Situation:** A 37-year old man presents for the first time to this primary care physician’s office to get a refill for his pain medication. He had a knee injury several years ago and has not been pain free since then.

You have already met this patient today and completed a pain assessment. You needed to step outside the exam room (reason is not relevant) and you are re-entering to complete the interview as described below.

**Setting**: Primary Care Clinic

**Your Tasks:**

1. Read the medical chart (initially unavailable), and screen and assess the patient for risk of prescription drug abuse. It is not necessary to give advice, refer the patient, or perform a physical examination. The focus is abuse of prescription drugs, not the injury per se.

Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine

Clinical Education Center

**MEDICAL CHART**

**Patient:** Charles White, Age 37

**CC:** Chronic knee pain due to an old football injury. Requests a refill of Percocet.

**HPI:**

* Fifteen years ago, patient injured right knee. States pain has never completely gone away. No recent re-injury.

**SH:**

* Married, 2 children
* Insurance adjuster, recently transferred, needs a new physician.

**Vital Signs:**

Height: \_\_\_\_\_\_

Weight: \_\_\_\_\_\_

Temperature: 101.7 degrees oral

Pulse: 97 per minute

Blood Pressure: 135/84

Respiratory Rate: 22

BMI: \_\_\_\_\_\_\_.

Allergies: Penicillin Medications

**PMH: (Information you received from earlier in the interview with the patient):**

While playing collegiate football, patient sustained an extensive, "career ending injury." Patient underwent four surgeries to restore mobility to the knee and then, what patient calls an ‘agonizing 18 months’ of physical therapy to restore partial use. He has not had any physical therapy since. Two years after the surgery he had steroidal injections and imaging of his knee. He tried acupuncture a year ago without much effect He still walks with a cane and experiences significant periods of pain which requires medication if he is to have any productivity that day. Without medication he states he is unable to work, socialize, or even concentrate for long periods.

He has tried Advil (600 mg every 4 hrs, about 12/day), which didn’t help. When he feels well he walks as much as he can with his cane for exercise and tries to be active with his children. He is currently taking Percocet (10mg/325mg [2 tablets 3x a day]) and has for the past 4 years.

**Pain Assessment done earlier in the interview:** Today, he stated the pain in his knee is moderate. He only has enough Percocet medication for three more days and he is afraid the pain will be severe if he runs out.

Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine

Clinical Education Center
private_patient_context:
**Instructions to Standardized Patient**

**Patient’s Name:** Charles White

**Presenting Situation:** The patient is a 37-year old man who recently moved to Chicago from Houston. He needs a new physician to prescribe him Percocet (a narcotic pain medication) for constant pain he has due to an old injury sustained 15 years ago from playing college football. He takes Percocet 3 times a day and has enough medication for three more days. For the patient this medication is a necessity; he cannot do without it. The patient knows it might be a crutch. The purpose and goal of this visit is only to get more Percocet prescribed. He feels that having to be evaluated is a demeaning waste of time.

* **Opening statement:** I was just transferred by my employer to Chicago and need a new physician to prescribe my pain medication. It took me a long time to find you and get an appointment, so I am almost out of pills. I only have 3 more days left.
* **Appearance and dress:** Wear casual business clothes. You need to look like you are in some pain. Have a cane by your chair (will be provided).
* **Mood/Affect/Emotions:** Look uncomfortable. Act irritated at times, especially if there is any resistance to getting the Percocet. If the clinician starts giving you too much advice, you can be unhappy or not ready to hear it.

**History of Present Illness:**

**Onset**: 15 years ago, I injured my right knee when I played college football. I was a running back. Once when I was tackled, my knee was injured and that was the end of my career. I had 4 operations and 18 months of physical therapy which was agonizing for me. My knee was never the same again and I walk with a cane. Also, the pain never went away completely.

**Location and quality**:

* The pain is in my right knee and sometimes goes up and down my leg.
* The pain feels manageable when I am on medication, even though it still hurts

**Characteristics/Intensity**:

* I’ve had pain for 15 years with a small decrease after the surgeries and physical therapy.
* I would describe my pain as moderate (3-4/10 on pain scale) when on the pain medicine.
* When I take Percocet (if have already revealed the name; if not say pain medicine), my pain is: 3-4 (1-10 pain scale). Without Percocet: 8 (1-10 pain scale).

**Aggravating/alleviating factors**: If I’m not on Percocet, it hurts all the time no matter what I do. Only the Percocet helps.

**Medications/Treatments**

* **Percocet**
* Dose:
  + I take 2 pills, 3 times a day. I take the Percocet in the morning, after work and in the evening. The pills are 10 mg/325 mg tablets.
  + If asked about a starting dose: I started with 1 pill three times a day, but now I take 2 pills three times a day.
  + I’ve been on the Percocet for the past 4 years.
  + How does the Percocet affect you?
    - It really helps. The pain never totally goes away, but at least I can work and function. I can concentrate better. It makes my life manageable and the only way I can live a halfway normal life.
    - Occasionally, I wake up in the morning with a sharp pain, but it subsides after I take Percocet.
  + Side effects:
    - I get constipated sometimes and could use a prescription for that.
    - I sometimes feel sleepy, but not often. I make sure I don’t drive. But I usually don’t have trouble with that
  + If asked why was the change made to Percocet: My doctor put me on the Percocet. It has fewer side effects (than the morphine – nausea and dizziness, sometimes).
  + Significance**:** Without the Percocet, I can’t do anything. I can’t concentrate enough to work and my knee hurts with any movement. I just need a new prescription for Percocet to manage my life.
* **Other treatments**
  + I had physical therapy for 18 agonizing months after my surgery
  + Two years after my surgery (13 years ago), I had steroids put in my knee with a needle
  + Six years ago, I tried Advil so I could get off prescription pain medicine. It didn’t help at all. I took 600mg tablets 4 times a day for about 1 week.
  + A year ago, I tried acupuncture. It only helped for a day and I never went back for more treatments.

**Other:** If asked about your knee: I can bend my knee a little bit, but not all the way

**Past Medical History**:

**Childhood and adult illnesses**: Own history. Last physical was a year ago.

**Hospitalizations and surgeries:** Only for my knee injury. The injury required four separate operations.

**Allergies:**

* Penicillin. Found that out when I was a kid. I broke out in a rash.
* I have seasonal allergies. I take Chlortrimeton occasionally for sinus congestion.

**Medications:**

* Morphine (only if asked):
  + I was given morphine immediately after my surgery while I was in the hospital. This was given to me intravenously.
  + Once I was home, I took the long acting release pill. I continued to take it until 4 years ago (total time on morphine pills was 11 years). ow my
  + If asked about the dose: I took 30 mg twice a day for the first four weeks after I got home. My dose was then lowered to 15 mg twice per day. Also, I started physical therapy about this time.
  + Side effects: I had some nausea and bad constipation. Sometimes I got dizzy and felt out of it. The dizziness lasted about 2 weeks. I was nauseous a few times a day the whole time I was on the morphine. It was mostly in the afternoon and evenings. I did my best to deal with it.
* Over-the-counter drugs:
  + Allergy medicine (Chlortrimeton) in the spring and fall
* **Other Specific pain medication information:**
  + **Have you ever taken more than the prescribed amount**? Yes, but just twice
    - Once after they reduced my prescription for long-acting morphine. I think I took 3-4 pills over the course of a week.
    - And 2 years ago when I had a particularly bad pain spell. I took an extra 3- 4 pills over the course of a week. Then my doctor increased the Percocet from one to two pills and it has been better.
  + **Have you ever tried to stop taking the pain medication?** Yes, only once
* I tried was 6 years ago. I wanted to try to stop because I didn’t like taking pain meds all the time. It didn’t last long. I wasn’t able to do anything normal, I didn’t feel well and I wasn’t able to sleep. I never made it more than a week.

**Life Style Behavioral Risks**:

* **Diet:** Own history. 3 cups of coffee a day.
* **Exercise:** My only exercise is walking, with a cane.
* **Sleep**: Sometimes I have trouble sleeping. The pain sometimes keeps me awake or wakes me up in the middle of the night and then I have trouble getting back to sleep. The pain that wakes me up is quite sharp and then I can’t get comfortable, no matter the position. But usually the Percocet helps that.
* **Stress**: Things seem really stressful right now--from moving, new job responsibilities, new schools for the kids, the pain in my knee, lack of sleep, tenseness in the relationship with my wife. My wife and I are getting short with each other because of all the changes in our lives.
* **Tobacco**: Don’t smoke; never have.
* **Alcohol:** I drink 1-2 beers maybe once a month, when my pain is bad after work or before bed. I know I shouldn’t drink, so it is only when the pain is worse and I don’t want to take more medication than I should. I did have a beer last night to help with all the stress I’ve been under.
* **Prescription drug use behavior:**
* I have had a few early refills (2, I think) because my pain was really bad. Last time, my doctor warned me that he would discontinue the medication if I did it again (about 2 years ago). He increased my dosage of Percocet so now I’m okay.
  + I have never over-sedated myself (put to sleep or knocked out)
  + I have never felt intoxicated
  + I have never gotten prescriptions from friends or more than one doctor at a time
* **Illegal drug use:** none
* **Sexual history:**
* **Current:** I’ve had a monogamous relationship with my wife for the past 10 years since my marriage.
* **Number of partners:**  Own history.
* **Birth Control:** Own history.
* **Sexually transmitted diseases:** Neither one of us have had a sexual illness
* **Sexual issues**: It hasn’t been great because of the stress of moving, my pain and medications. My desire for sex and ability to "perform" have decreased.
* **Legal Issues:** I have never had legal problems or been arrested due to drug or alcohol use or anything else.

**Psychological History:**

* **Age:** 37 (Sept 10, 1974)
* **Marital/Parental status**: I've been married for ten years. We have two children (a boy 8 yrs. and a girl 6 yrs.).
* **Occupation**: I’m an insurance adjuster for a national insurance company. I just moved to the Midwest from Houston about one month ago when I was transferred to a regional branch.
* **Where do you live?** Chicago.
* **Mental Health**:
  + **Depression:** I feel down sometimes because I’ve had pain for such a long time and I’ve taken meds for so long. The depression never lasts for more than a day or two. My wife and kids help pull me out of it.
  + **Treatment:** I’ve never had treatment for depression or felt I needed it.
  + **Suicidal thoughts:** No. I’ve never thought about hurting myself.
  + **History of preadolescent sexual abuse:** None

**Family History**:

* **Mother:** 68; alive and well
  + If asked about alcohol of drug abuse: My mother doesn’t drink or use illegal drugs
* **Father:** 69; alive and well
  + If asked about alcohol of drug abuse: My father drinks socially, but isn’t an alcoholic. Doesn’t use illegal drugs.
* **Siblings:** None
* **Family Health:** No family history of any health problems.

**MONITORING QUESTIONS:**

**Urine Screening:** If asked if you’d be willing to have urine drug screening: I suppose so if I have to in order to get the Percocet but I’m not happy about it. Can I get a temporary prescription until I come back for the next appointment?

**Records from Texas Physician:** If asked about getting records from your doctor in Texas: Go ahead, but that will take so long, won’t it? I really need the medication now. Please, can I have a temporary prescription?

**Signing an Agreement**: If asked to sign an agreement (one doctor, one pharmacy, no early refills, etc.): I think it’s demeaning, but if I have to, I will.

**Other Pain Management Options**: If asked to consider other pain management options: (Be reluctant) I’ve tried a lot of things, but they never help or not for long. I’ve tried things like acupuncture and physical therapy. My doctor in Texas understood that all of it just didn’t work as well as the medications.

Summary: TimeLine for Treatment

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

turns.content: Thanks for waiting, Mr. White. I ask everyone taking opioid pain medicine a few safety questions. Over the past four years, have you ever taken more Percocet than prescribed or run out early? Have you obtained pain medication from any other doctors, emergency rooms, friends, or other sources?

I have had a few early refills because my pain was really bad. I did take a little extra Percocet a couple of times when the pain was really bad. But I've never gotten prescriptions from friends or more than one doctor at a time.

I appreciate your honesty. When you took extra, did you ever feel unable to cut back or find yourself craving Percocet? Have you ever used it for reasons other than knee pain—such as to relax, sleep, or change your mood?
No, I didn't feel like I couldn't cut back. I just took a little extra when the pain was really bad. I only use it for the knee pain. I haven't used it for any other reason.

Thank you. For safety, do you drink alcohol or use marijuana or other recreational drugs? Are you taking any sleeping pills, anti-anxiety medicines such as Xanax, or other sedating medications along with Percocet?
I drink 1-2 beers maybe once a month, when my pain is bad after work or before bed. I don't use any other recreational drugs. I'm not taking any sleeping pills or anti-anxiety medicines.

Thank you—that’s helpful. Two last questions: if you miss or delay a dose, do you develop symptoms such as sweating, shakiness, nausea, diarrhea, or marked restlessness? And has your Percocet use ever caused problems at work or home, or led family members to express concern?
I don't think I've ever missed a dose. I take it regularly. I haven't had any problems at work or home because of the Percocet. My family hasn't said anything about it.
